newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open mixed, PGMs up.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open mixed, PGMs up.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were called to open mixed Thursday, with little change expected in gold and silver, but platinum and palladium were set to surge following further sharp, overnight gains.

NYMEX July platinum was called to open $7.00 to $13.00 an ounce higher from Wednesday's close of $411.60. On overnight ACCESS July surged $11.40 higher to $423.00. September palladium was due to open $6.00 to $7.00 an ounce firmer.
The lack of available spot supplies and soaring lease rates continued to push prices higher, traders said.

In London platinum was fixed at $440 an ounce, its highest since September 15, 1995, while palladium was fixed at $235.00 an ounce, its highest since twice-daily fixing began in 1989 and its highest spot price since early 1980.
There was great interest in the role of a leading U.S. hedge fund which reportedly has a huge long palladium position, and how this could be unwound without causing prices to plunge.
In gold, overnight dealings were muted as the market, along with silver, was sidelined as the focus remained on the white metals.
COMEX August gold contract set to open flat to off $0.50 an ounce, traded $344.30 to $343.00 an ounce in overnight ACCESS dealings.
Gold was fixed in London Thursday morning at $340.70 an ounce, off $1.05 from Wednesday afternoon.
COMEX July silver was set to open unchanged from Wednesday's close at $4.70 an ounce.
COMEX gold stocks were unchanged Wednesday while silver stocks rose 795,880 ounces to 202,478,201.
The jobless claims for week ended May 31, forecast at 320,000 compared to 322,000 in the previous week, were due at 0830 EDT.
